Gloria Mundi.

Our material, however, is not bought from any shop, yet it is found there daily, and shopkeepers throw it into the streets. It suffices, therefore, that it is found for free: but the material of our <term>stone</term> is compared to all those things with which the craftsmen labor: for our stone is our <term>salt</term>, our <term>mercury</term>, <term>verdigris</term>, <term>saltpeter</term>, <term>sal ammoniac</term>, <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note>, <term>sulfur</term>, and infinite others of that kind, yet not dug up from wild and rural mountains with hammers and other instruments: but our stone is drawn only from our own mountains and springs: in our <term>salt-spring</term> our <term>salt</term> is found: from our earth our metal, <term>mercury</term>, and <term>sulfur</term> are poured, and not from wild, foreign, or rural mountains, all of which the craftsmen do not understand, nor can they believe or grasp them; for the Lord has obscured and stopped their senses, and because of this they used these things otherwise than they ought to have been used, and did not aim at the target in the least, yet they nevertheless persisted in this contrary sense, and indulged their own stubborn heads; for when they should have <term>distilled</term> gently, there they <term>sublimed</term> with a strong fire, they burned <term>aqua fortis</term> <gloss>strong water/nitric acid</gloss>, and they instantly burned the operation of nature and its substances, and reduced them to nothing. Also, when they should have <term>dissolved</term>, there they <term>coagulated</term>, and again, as if unskilled in things, they handled the matter unskillfully, and fell into doubt, and with lying words they declared the art to be not true but false, in which, however, they themselves rightly lie: for their own ignorance shamefully deceived them, which must be imputed to their own obscure and murky cunning, while, according to their own dark intellect, they interpreted words otherwise than they sounded. For example, when the Philosophers spoke of <term>calcining</term> (which they call grinding), then those unskilled <term>philosophasters</term> <gloss>would-be philosophers</gloss> understood it as burning, and reduced the substances entirely to ashes, so that nothing could be made from them. <summary>This page critiques the errors of unskilled practitioners who misunderstand alchemical texts, arguing that they use common shop-bought minerals and destructive processes like intense heat instead of the gentle, natural methods described by true Philosophers.</summary>
